correctness.rationale: All fourteen nonempty sign cells arise from positive dependence of normals and elementary sign patterns. Spherical excess gives two A triangles, six B triangles, six C quadrilaterals. The exact derivative ratio ρ=2√3t/√(1+3t²) and its strict monotonicity prove the A=B and C=A switches and C>B. Strict integral average inequalities establish global monotonicity of M/m. The checker independently enumerates actual spherical polygons and passes nine configurations plus 9,999 numerical monotonic samples; sampling is corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: The mathematical claim is the complete parameter-dependent area spectrum, largest/smallest area ratio and a second largest-cell transition in a specified threefold-symmetric four-great-circle family. This is not implied by the recorded global maximum of the smallest four-circle cell area, and the motivating 2026 article proves only sufficiently-large-number bounds. The surveyed references and semantic comparisons do not exhibit an equivalent full profile. Historical priority is provisional.
residual_risks: The full original 1958 paper of Heppes was not obtained; its scope is grounded in a scholarly survey rather than primary inspection.
The complete text of Bezdek–Lángi arXiv:2201.11234 was inaccessible through available routes; its abstract and indexed theorem indicate a different invariant.
A mathematically equivalent less-searchable parameterization could exist in older literature; absence from retrieval is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The sharp largest/smallest cell-area ratio is a named open-ended spherical arrangement objective. Its complete exact dependence on a natural one-parameter threefold-symmetry class, including full fourteen-cell spectrum, equality, a second max-cell bifurcation, and divergent extreme limits, is a motivated geometric benchmark not furnished by the older isolated smallest-area equality. The restricted nature is explicit and no unsupported global result is claimed.
